subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up — token volumes / target $/1M
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Model mix & pricing follow-up — token volumes / target $/1M

Alex — great to speak earlier, thanks for the time. Quick recap + a few asks so we can build a clear pricing estimate and next steps: 

Call recap (quick):
- Brightlayer plans to add LLM features into customer support workflows (resolution summarization + knowledge search) and an embeddings-powered similarity search for internal docs.
- Primary users: internal CS agents + a subset of clients via API. Expected growth over 6–9 months.

To put together a concrete cost estimate and recommended model mix, can you confirm the following (rough numbers are fine):
1) Monthly token volumes (approx): chat/generation tokens per month, embeddings vector units / requests, and any re-rank / reranking token counts. If you have per-feature splits (e.g., agent summarization vs. customer-facing generation) that helps.
2) Target monthly budget range (e.g., $Xk–$Yk) or target unit economics in $/1M tokens.
3) SLA/latency expectations (p99 <100ms, <500ms, etc.) and whether you need dedicated capacity or are ok starting on hosted.

If you prefer, send a quick spreadsheet and I’ll turn it into a model-level cost estimate. I’ll also include a short set of options: hosted API PoC, short Dedicated reserved pool (pilot), and a cost/latency tradeoff with quantization suggestions.

Next steps we recommend:
- You share ballpark token volumes & budget — we draft model-level estimates and a PoC scope (2–4 weeks).
- If procurement is involved, we’ll include an initial SOW and standard terms.

Attaching: blank token-estimate template I use (I can fill it out if you prefer).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

(415) 555-0192

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightlayer.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightlayer Procurement <procurement@brightlayer.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 18:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up — token volumes / target $/1M

Thanks Marissa — good call. Quick answers below (rough, happy to refine):

1) Volumes (month 1 / steady-state estimate):
- Chat/generation (agent summaries, small customer replies): ~10M input+output tokens / month
- Embeddings (semantic search for docs + knowledge base): ~2M vector operations / month (embedding size 1536)
- Rerank (when we do top-K re-scoring): ~500k token ops / month

Rough per-feature split: agent summarization ~70% of chat tokens, customer-facing generation ~30%.

2) Budget: target $50k–$75k / month to start. If you can provide a target $/1M tokens we can map to our internal forecasts — aiming for ~ $1,200–$1,800 per 1M tokens total blended across model types.

3) Latency: for agent workflows p95 <250ms is preferred; customer-facing generation can tolerate up to ~1s. Initially hosted is fine but we want the option for Dedicated within 2–3 months if numbers justify it.

Regarding quantization: we’d be open to 8-bit/4-bit if it keeps latency low without obvious quality regressions.

I’ll loop in procurement once we have an indicative cost.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
VP Product, Brightlayer
alex.johnson@brightlayer.com
+1 720-555-0123

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Model mix & pricing follow-up — token volumes / target $/1M

Thanks for the details — super helpful. Drafting up a couple of model-level pricing scenarios and a blended estimate based on the volumes you gave. Summary of what I’ll include in the estimate (attached as an XLSX):

Assumptions / proposed model mix for the estimate:
- Chat/generation: 80% of token volume served by an efficient chat model (gpt-chat-13b-q4 or similar quantized variant) and 20% routed to higher-quality chat model for customer-facing flows.
- Embeddings: use an optimized 1536-d embedding model (embed-1536-finetuned), majority served on quantized CPU/GPU path.
- Rerank: use a small cross-encoder reranker (rerank-1.3b) for top-K scoring; kept as a smaller portion of cost.

Per-model volume split (based on your numbers):
- Chat/generation: 10M tokens (approx) — assume 85% agent summarization + 15% customer-facing generation for the routing split above.
- Embeddings: 2M vectors (~2M requests)
- Rerank: 0.5M token ops

Unit economics (initial ballpark):
- Chat (quantized chat model): $1,200 per 1M tokens
- Chat (higher-quality): $3,500 per 1M tokens
- Embeddings (per 1M vectors/requests): $200 per 1M (vector generation cost — numbered as embedding unit pricing)
- Rerank (per 1M tokens): $800 per 1M tokens

Blended estimate (approx):
- Chat: 10M tokens blended at (0.8*$1,200 + 0.2*$3,500) = $1,540 per 1M => ~ $15,400/month
- Embeddings: 2M units at $200 per 1M => ~$400/month
- Rerank: 0.5M at $800 per 1M => ~$400/month
- Estimated total hosted cost: ~$16.2k/month (note: these are model-only inference costs and don’t include data retention, ingress/egress, or dedicated-reservation premiums)

Given your stated target budget $50k–$75k, there’s room to expand usage (or adopt higher-quality routing) and still be within budget. If you want to hit the $50–75k band with current volumes we can:
- Move more customer-facing traffic to the higher-quality model (increases blended $/1M)
- Add a Dedicated reserved pool (reduces per-token cost for high steady-state throughput)
- Introduce caching/prefix reuse for agent summarization where appropriate (reduces token volume)

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll attach a filled pricing_estimate XLSX with line-item math (attached).
2) Vivek — can you take a look at the Dedicated-savings scenario and a 6-month reserved commitment delta?
3) Alex — if you confirm procurement contact, I’ll send a short SOW + initial T&Cs for review (we’ll include a 30-day pilot option).

Attaching: redwood_pricing_estimate.xlsx (filled).

Thanks,
Marissa
